types.embedding_query_text: Company: An organization that produces goods or services, typically on a large scale. Also called corporation, firm, enterprise, business, vendor. Examples: Microsoft, Activision-Blizzard.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: Matches companies like Microsoft and Activision‑Blizzard

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

types.embedding_query_text: ProductDivision: A distinct business unit or brand within a larger company, focusing on a specific product line. Also called division, unit, subsidiary, brand, segment. Examples: Xbox.

chosen_type.label: ProductDivision
chosen_type.definition: A distinct business unit within a larger company that focuses on a specific product line or brand.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class captures a business unit/brand division

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: ProductCollection
candidates.comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, figure, character, personage. Examples: Amy Coleman, Asha Sharma.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: GameStudio: A company that develops video games. Also called developer, studio, game developer, production house, creator. Examples: Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory, Undead Lab.

chosen_type.label: GameStudio
chosen_type.definition: A company or organizational unit that develops video games.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class represents a video‑game development studio

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: GameServer
candidates.comment: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

types.embedding_query_text: Analyst: A professional who evaluates and comments on industry trends and company performance. Also called commentator, expert, pundit, observer, specialist. Examples: Paolo Pescatore, Piers Harding-Rolls.

chosen_type.label: Analyst
chosen_type.definition: A professional who evaluates and comments on industry trends, market data, or company performance.
chosen_type.justification: Analyst is a role of a person, not covered by existing schema.org classes

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

candidates.label: CriticReview
candidates.comment: A CriticReview is a professionally written and in-depth evaluation of a creative work, product, or service, published by a recognized reviewing source. Also called professional review, expert review, critical assessment, published critique. Examples: A movie review by a film critic, a restaurant review in a food guide, a book review in a literary magazine. Distinct from UserReview, which is a casual review written by a customer or general user.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: Comment
candidates.comment: A textual remark or observation made about an item, such as a blog post. Also called remark, feedback, note, annotation. Examples: A user's comment on a YouTube video, a review on a product page, a blog post comment, a code comment.

candidates.label: ReviewNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A specialized news article that combines factual reporting with a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic work. Also called critical news report, professional review article, news critique. Examples: a New York Times review of a Broadway show, a tech blog's assessment of a new smartphone, a music magazine's album critique.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific calendar day. Also called day, calendar date, point in time, specific date, timestamp. Examples: 2026-07-06, Monday, 2024, 2019.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are specific calendar dates or years

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

types.embedding_query_text: Role Examples: Executive Vice President, Chief Executive.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are job titles within an organization

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.
